Let us focus on the second inequality. We have
	\[ \mu_{\mathsf{null}}(\mathcal E) = \mathbf{E}_{\mathsf{pl}} \left[ \boldsymbol{1}_{\mathcal E} \cdot \frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{null}}}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}} \right] \leqslant \sqrt{ \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}(\mathcal E)  } \cdot \sqrt{ \mathbf{E}_{\mathsf{pl}} \left[ \left(\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{null}}}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}}\right)^2 \right] } = \sqrt{ \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}(\mathcal E)  } \cdot \sqrt{ \mathbf{E}_{\mathsf{null}} \left[ \frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{null}}}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}} \right] } \,. \]
	It remains to show that second quantity is $O(1)$. Note now that for any prescribed interaction matrix $W$ (without the scaling by $\beta$),
	\begin{align*}
		\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{null}}}(W \mid {\boldsymbol{x}} = x) &= \frac{ \exp\left( - \frac{N}{4} \left\| W - \frac{\beta}{N} xx^\top \right\|_{F}^2 \right) }{{ \exp\left( - \frac{N}{4} \|W\|_{F}^2 \right) }} \propto \exp\left( \frac{\beta}{2} x^\top W x \right) \,, \text{so} \\
		\frac{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{pl}}}{\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu_{\mathsf{null}}}(W) &\propto \sum_{x \in \{\pm 1\}^N} \exp\left( \frac{\beta}{2} x^\top W x \right) = Z_{\beta W} \,.
	\end{align*}
	Our goal is then simply to show that
	\[ \mathbf{E} \left[\frac{1}{Z_{\beta\boldsymbol{W}}}\right] \lesssim \frac{1}{\mathbf{E}[Z_{\beta\boldsymbol{W}}]} \,. \]
	This estimate is easily obtained by integrating the lower tail described in \cite[Theorem 11.2.1]{Tal11}. The first inequality is similar and requires us to show that $\mathbf{E}[Z_{\beta\boldsymbol{W}}^2] \lesssim \mathbf{E}[Z_{\beta\boldsymbol{W}}]^2$, which is far easier to establish.

We need the following stronger version of \Cref{th:cov-bounds} and prove that for any constant $a > 0$:

label: lem:organized-diagonal
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:organized-diagonal}
	We have
	\(
		(K\mathbf{Cov}-\mathrm{Id})_{ii}
		=\lambda_i v_i-\frac{2\beta^2m_i}{N}(\mathbf{Cov} m)_i\,.
	\)
	Further, for every $a>0$ we have:
	\[
		\mathbf{Pr}\left[\max_{i\in[N]}|\lambda_i|>N^{-1/4}\right]
		\leqslant O(N^{-a}).
	\]
	Hence,
	\[
		\max_{i\in[N]}
		\left|(K\mathbf{Cov}-\mathrm{Id})_{ii}-\lambda_i v_i\right|
		\leqslant 2\beta^2.
	\]
head: environment
name: Diagonal terms

title: Proof
body_md:
We begin by conditioning on the high probability events from
		\Cref{lem:organized-off-diagonal,lem:organized-diagonal,lem:organized-gap}, which simultaneously hold with probability $1-O(N^{-a})$.
		Now define
		\[
			D=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i),
			\qquad R=(K-D)\mathbf{Cov}-\mathrm{Id}.
		\]
		Then we have
		\[
			\left\|R-\operatorname{diag}(R)\right\|_F^2 = \sum_{i=1}^N \|f_i - \lambda_i \mathbf{Cov}_{-i,i}\|_2^2 \leqslant C\,.
		\]
		By the identity in \Cref{lem:organized-diagonal} and the fact that $\mathbf{Cov}_{ii}=v_i$, we have for all $i$ that
		\[ |R_{ii}| = \left| (K \mathbf{Cov} - \mathrm{Id})_{ii} - (D \mathbf{Cov})_{ii} \right| \leqslant \left| (\lambda_i v_i + 2\beta^2) - (\lambda_i (1-m_i^2)) \right| = 2\beta^2 \,, \]
		and consequently,
		\[
			\|R\|_{\mathrm{op}}
			\leqslant
			\|R-\operatorname{diag}(R)\|_F
			+\max_i|R_{ii}|
			\leqslant O(1)\,.
		\]
		Noting now that $K \succeq \gamma$ for some constant $\gamma$, and $D \preceq o(1)$, this implies that $\left\|\mathbf{Cov}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}} = O(1)$, and thus \Cref{lem:organized-residual,cor:organized-covariance}.

label: eq:silly-bound-on-K-lipschitzness
title: Proof
body_md:
Define the set of ``good'' disorder $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}$ by
			\[ \mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}} = \left\{ (W,g) : \text{for all $u$ with $\|\widehat{m}(W,g) - u\| \leqslant 2 \varepsilon \sqrt{N}$, $K_{W,g}(u) \succeq 2\gamma$} \right\} \,, \]
			so $\mathbf{Pr}\left[ \mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}} \right] \geqslant 1/2$ by \Cref{lem:mid-probability-pred-bound}(b). First, observe that by definition,
			\begin{equation}
				\label{eq:silly-bound-on-K-lipschitzness}
				\|K_{W,g}(u) - K_{W',g'}(u) \|_2 \leqslant \| W - W' \|_2 \,.
			\end{equation}
			Suppose that we want to establish that $K_{W,g}(m)$ is bounded away from $0$. Further suppose that we had, for some $(W',g') \in \mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}$, that
			\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
				\item $\|W - W'\|_{2} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \|g - g'\|_2 \leqslant \gamma$,
				\item $\|m(W,g) - \widehat{m}(W,g)\| \leqslant \varepsilon\sqrt{N}$, and
				\item $\|\widehat{m}(W,g) - \widehat{m}(W',g')\| \leqslant \varepsilon\sqrt{N}$.
			\end{enumerate}
			This would complete the proof. Indeed, (ii) and (iii) imply that $\|m(W,g) - \widehat{m}(W',g')\| \leqslant 2\varepsilon\sqrt{N}$, so the definition of $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}$ gives that $K_{W',g'}(m(W,g)) \succeq 2\gamma$. \eqref{eq:silly-bound-on-K-lipschitzness} then implies that $K_{W,g}(m(W,g)) \succeq K_{W',g'}(m(W,g)) - \| W - W' \|_{2} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \|g - g'\|_2 \succeq \gamma$, as desired.

			It remains to show that the three conditions hold with high probability.
			(ii) holds with probability $1 - N^{-a}$ by \Cref{lem:mid-probability-pred-bound}(a), and the Lipschitzness of \Cref{lem:mid-probability-pred-bound}(c) reduces (iii) to a statement like (i). To conclude, it suffices to establish that for any small constant $\eta$, with high probability over $\boldsymbol{W}$, there exists $(W',g') \in \mathcal E_{\mathrm{good}}$ such that $\|W - W'\| + \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \|g-g'\| \leqslant \eta$. This in fact occurs with probability $1 - e^{-cN}$ using Gaussian isoperimetry, e.g. \cite[Theorem 10.15]{BLM13}---this implies that for any set $S$ of standard Gaussian measure at least $1/2$, $\mathbf{Pr}_{\boldsymbol{g} \sim \mathcal N\left(0,1\right)}\left[ \inf_{x \in S} \|\boldsymbol{g} - x\| \geqslant r \right] \leqslant e^{-r^2/2}$, completing the proof.

Let $\mathcal D = (\boldsymbol{M} , \boldsymbol{h})$, so $m = \mathbf{E}[ {\boldsymbol{x}} \mid \mathcal D ]$. That is,
			\[ \frac{m^\top \widehat{m}}{N} = \mathbf{E}\left[ \frac{{\boldsymbol{x}}^\top \widehat{m}}{N} \mid \mathcal D \right] \,. \]
			                                                   
			For any fixed iterate $k$, \cite[Proposition 3]{Cel24} establishes that $\frac{{\boldsymbol{x}}^\top \widehat{m}}{N} \to q_{k}$ in probability, for some explicit constant $q_{k}$. Consider the random variable $\rho = \frac{{\boldsymbol{x}}^\top \widehat{m}}{N}$, conditioned on ${\boldsymbol{x}}$, defined in terms of the disorder $\boldsymbol{W}$ and the noise in the external field $\boldsymbol{g}$. Using the Kirszbraun extension theorem and the Lipschitzness of (c), we may define a function $\widetilde{m}$ that is $O(\sqrt{N})$-Lipschitz in $W$ everywhere, and $\widetilde{m} = \widehat{m}$ with probability $1 - e^{-cN}$. Define $\widetilde{\rho} = \frac{{\boldsymbol{x}}^\top \widetilde{m}}{N}$. Gaussian concentration yields that
			\[ \mathbf{Pr}\left[ | \widetilde{\rho} - \mathbf{E} \widetilde{\rho} | > s \right] \leqslant e^{-cNs^2} \,, \]
			and $\rho \to q_{k}$ in probability also implies that for sufficiently large $k$, for constant $\delta$,

			\[ \mathbf{Pr}\left[ \left| \frac{m^\top \widehat{m}}{N} - q_{k} \right| \geqslant \delta \right] \leqslant e^{-cN} \]
			To conclude, we write
			\[ \frac{\| m - \widehat{m} \|^2}{N} = \frac{\|m\|^2}{N} + \frac{\|\widehat{m}\|^2}{N} - 2 \cdot \frac{\widehat{m}^\top m}{N} \,. \]

			\[ - v^\top \widetilde{K}(u) v = \beta v^\top \boldsymbol{W} v + R(u,v) \,, \]

			\[ \operatorname{plimsup}_{N \to \infty} \sup_{u,v} \left\{ \beta v^\top \boldsymbol{W} v + R(u,v) \right\} \leqslant \operatorname{plimsup}_{N \to \infty} \sup_{u,v} \left\{ \frac{2\beta}{\sqrt{N}} \left\langle g_{\mathrm{AMP}}(v) , v \right\rangle + R(u,v)\right\} \]

Let $\boldsymbol{I} \sim [N]$ be a random index, and define $M = \widehat{m}_{\boldsymbol{I}}$, $U = u_{\boldsymbol{I}}$, and $V = \sqrt{N} v_{\boldsymbol{I}}$. The extra rank-one term $\frac{2\beta^2}{N} \langle v , \widehat{m} \rangle^2$ is then precisely $2\beta^2 \mathbf{E}[MV]^2$. 
			                                                                                                                                                              
			                                                        
			                                         
			Assume wlog that ${\boldsymbol{x}} = \boldsymbol{1}$.

			The next step is to move to appropriate \textit{limiting} distributions for all these random variables. At the cost of some small error $\delta_{k}$ that goes to $0$ as the iterate $k$ (defining $\widehat{m}$), this allows us to work with idealized distributions that are explicitly defined in terms of Gaussians. For example, we can pretend that $M$ is distributed as $\tanh\left( t+\beta^2q + \boldsymbol{z} \sqrt{t+\beta^2 q} \right)$ for $\boldsymbol{z} \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$, up to some small error.

			The upshot, which is the content of \cite[Sections 4.2--4.4]{Cel24}, is essentially \cite[Eq. (26)]{Cel24} with an extra term corresponding to the rank-one part. This is as follows.
			\[ \mathcal J(U,V) = 2\beta\mathbf{E}[B_{\rho} V] - \mathbf{E}\left[ \frac{V^2}{1 - U^2} \right] + \beta^2 (\mathbf{E}[V])^2 - \beta^2 (1 - q) + \underbrace{2\beta^2 q \rho^2}_{\text{new term}} \,, \]
			where we have the constraints
			\[ \mathbf{E}[V^2] = 1 \,, \qquad |U| \leqslant 1 \,, \qquad \mathbf{E}[SV] = \rho\sqrt{q} \,, \qquad \|U-S\|_{2} \leqslant \varepsilon + \delta_{k} \]
			and for some choice of $\boldsymbol{z}_1,\boldsymbol{z}_2,\boldsymbol{z}_3 \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$ that are independent from each other,
			\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				S &= \tanh\left( t+\beta^2q + \boldsymbol{z}_1 \beta\sqrt{q} + \boldsymbol{z}_2 \sqrt{t} \right) \,, \\
				B_{\rho} &= \rho \boldsymbol{z}_1 +  \boldsymbol{z}_3 \sqrt{1 - \rho^2} \,.
			\end{aligned}
			\label{eq:s-brho-definitions}
			\end{equation}
			In particular, $\mathbf{E}[S^2] = q$, and $\rho = \frac{\mathbf{E}[SV]}{\sqrt{q}} \in [-1,1]$. Here, $\boldsymbol{S}$ plays the role of the typical coordinate of $\widehat{m}$. The next step is to also replace the $\boldsymbol{U}$ with $\boldsymbol{S}$, suffering a small constant loss.

			Towards this, we have for any choice of $a,b,\alpha$ that
			\begin{align*}
				\mathcal J &= 2\beta\mathbf{E}[B_{\rho} V] - \mathbf{E}\left[ \frac{V^2}{1 - U^2} \right] + \beta^2 (\mathbf{E}[V])^2 - \beta^2 (1 - q) + 2\beta^2 q \rho^2 \\
				&\qquad\qquad + a \left( \frac{\mathbf{E}[SV]}{\sqrt{q}} - \rho \right) + b\left( \mathbf{E}[V] - \mathbf{E}[V] \right) + \alpha\left( \mathbf{E}[V^2] - 1 \right) \\
					&= \mathbf{E}\left[ V \left( 2\beta B_{\rho} + \frac{aS}{\sqrt{q}} + b \right) - V^2 \left(\frac{1}{1 - U^2} -  \alpha \right) \right] \\
					&\qquad\qquad + \beta^2 (\mathbf{E}[V])^2 - \beta^2 (1 - q) + 2\beta^2 q \rho^2 - a\rho - b\mathbf{E}[V] - \alpha \\
					&\leqslant \frac{1}{4} \mathbf{E}\left[ \frac{ \left( 2\beta B_{\rho} + \frac{aS}{\sqrt{q}} + b \right)^2 }{ \frac{1}{1-U^2} - \alpha } \right] + \beta^2 (\mathbf{E}[V])^2 - \beta^2 (1 - q) + 2\beta^2 q \rho^2 - a\rho - b\mathbf{E}[V] - \alpha \,.
			\end{align*}
			The final inequality here is by the AM-GM inequality: we have $cv - dv^2 \leqslant \frac{c^2}{4d}$. Note now that if $0 \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 1/2$, we may replace $\boldsymbol{U}$ with $\boldsymbol{S}$ in the first expression, at the cost of a small loss. After doing this, we are left with an extremely explicit calculation in terms of Gaussians, since essentially all dependence on $\boldsymbol{V}$ has been removed. Now denote $\eta = \mathbf{E}[V]$.

			The result is a modification \cite[Eq. (27)]{Cel24}, which asks to show that
			\[ \inf_{0 \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 1/2} \mathcal L_\alpha \coloneqq \inf_{\substack{a,b \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}} \\ 0 \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 1/2}} \frac{1}{4} \mathbf{E}\left[ \frac{ \left( 2\beta B_{\rho} + \frac{aS}{\sqrt{q}} + b \right)^2 }{ \frac{1}{1-S^2} - \alpha } \right] + \beta^2 \eta^2 - \beta^2 (1 - q) + 2\beta^2 q \rho^2 - a\rho - b\eta - \alpha \]
			is negatively bounded away from $0$. In fact, it will suffice to show that $\mathcal L_0 \leqslant 0$---the remainder of the proof follows \cite[Section 4.4]{Cel24}, which uses a simple continuity argument to transform this to a strict negative margin by setting $\alpha$ to be a small positive constant.
			To do this, we set $a = 2\beta^2(2q\rho - \eta\sqrt{q})$ and $b = 2\beta^2\eta$. This then simplifies to
			\[ \mathcal L_0 \leqslant - \beta^2 (1 - \beta^2 \nu) \left( q\rho^2 + (\eta - \rho\sqrt{q})^2 \right) \,, \]
			for $\nu = \mathbf{E}[1-S^2]$. We omit the details of this calculation---it amounts to integrating out $\boldsymbol{z}_3$, using Gaussian integration by parts to explicitly compute terms like $\mathbf{E}[(1-S^2) \boldsymbol{z}_1^2]$ (which show up when expanding out the parenthesised terms in the expectation), and completing appropriate squares---such calculations are very similar to those done in \cite[pages 16 and 17]{Cel24}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume without loss of generality that ${\boldsymbol{x}} = \boldsymbol{1}$. We start by noting that \cite[Lemma 2.3]{BER26} holds for sufficiently large localization time. Indeed, choose $\delta$ such that the first condition of \cite[Theorem 1.1]{BER26} is satisfied, and every small submatrix has sufficiently small operator norm, which occurs with probability $1 - e^{-cN}$. The external field is of the form $T{\boldsymbol{x}} + \boldsymbol{g}\sqrt{T}$, For sufficiently large $T$, with probability $1 - e^{-cN}$, we have $\|\boldsymbol{g}\sqrt{T}\| \ll T\sqrt{N}$. Consequently, a sample from this measure has at least $\left( 1 - \frac{\delta}{2} \right)N$ positive spins, which by \cite[Lemma 2.2]{BER26} yields a correlation bound (for the base model as well as the pinned models).

    To conclude, we use this correlation bound until we have pinned $(1-\delta)N$ of the coordinates, and we are left with an Ising model (with some external field) whose interaction matrix has bounded spectral radius; \cite[Corollary 51]{CE22} yields a Poincar\'{e}~ inequality for these measures, and the spectral independence framework allows us to lift this back to a Poincar\'{e}~ inequality for $\mu_{T}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Taylor's theorem, the remainder term admits the following description:
    \begin{align*}
        \Delta_{d,i}
        &=
        \frac{\beta^5}{48}\int_0^1(1-s)^4
        \bigl(\kappa_{6,s}^{(i)}+\kappa_{6,-s}^{(i)}\bigr)
        [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes5}]\,ds,\\
        \Delta_{\mathbf{Cov},i}\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}
        &=
        \frac{\beta^3m_i}{4}\int_0^1(1-s)^2
        \bigl(\kappa_{5,s}^{(i)}+\kappa_{5,-s}^{(i)}\bigr)
        [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes4}]\,ds\\
        &\quad+
        \frac{\beta^4}{12}\int_0^1(1-s)^3
        \bigl(\kappa_{6,s}^{(i)}+\kappa_{6,-s}^{(i)}\bigr)
        [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes5}]\,ds\,.
    \end{align*}
    By \Cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} and triangle inequality, we have:
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\norm*{ \Delta_{d,i} }_F^p \leqslant C N^{-p},\qquad \mathbf{E}\norm*{ \Delta_{\mathbf{Cov},i} \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i} }_F^p \leqslant C N^{-3p/4}\,.
    \]
    The conclusion follows by applying Markov's inequality to the above for an appropriately large choice of $p$ depending on $\varepsilon$.

title: Remark
body_md:
To clarify the notation, for $q=2,3,4$, $\kappa^{(B)}_q$ is a tensor of order $q$, and $K^{(B)}$ acts by matrix multiplication on the first coordinate of $\kappa^{(B)}_q$: 
\[
(K^{(B)}\kappa^{(B)}_q)_{i j_1\cdots j_{q-1}}
= \sum_{a\notin B} K^{(B)}_{ia}(\kappa^{(B)}_q)_{a j_1\cdots j_{q-1}}.
\]
For $q = 1,2,3$, $\nabla^q r^{(B)}$ is a tensor of order $q+1$, where the first coordinate indexes the entries of $r^{(B)}$ while the remaining $q$ coordinates index the $q$ derivatives.
Similarly, $D^q T^{(B)}(m)$ is a tensor of order $q+1$ where the first coordinate indexes the entries of $T^{(B)}$.
In the notation $D^2 T^{(B)}(m)\{\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)},\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}$, the matrices $\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}$ act by matrix multiplication on all but the first coordinate of $D^2 T^{(B)}(m)$:
\[
\left(D^2T^{(B)}(m)\{\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)},\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}\right)_{ijk}
=
\sum_{a,b\notin B}
\frac{\partial^2T_i^{(B)}}{\partial z_a\partial z_b}(m)
\,\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}_{aj}\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}_{bk},
\]
We define $D^3 T^{(B)}(m) \{\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)},\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)},\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}$ similarly.
In $D^2T^{(B)}(m)\{\kappa^{(B)}_3,\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}$, $\kappa^{(B)}_3$ and $\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}$ contract with all but the first coordinates of $D^2 T^{(B)}(m)$:
\[
    \left(D^2T^{(B)}(m)\{\kappa^{(B)}_3,\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}\right)_{ijk\ell}
    = \sum_{a,b\notin B}
    \frac{\partial^2T_i^{(B)}}{\partial z_a\partial z_b}(m)
    (\kappa^{(B)}_3)_{ajk}\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}_{b\ell}\,.
\]
Finally, $\sum_{\mathsf{Sym}}$ sums cyclically over the last three coordinates of the resulting $4$-tensor:
\[
    \left(\sum_{\mathsf{Sym}}D^2T^{(B)}(m)\{\kappa^{(B)}_3,\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}\right)_{ijk\ell}
    = \sum_{abc \in \{jk\ell, k\ell j, \ell jk\}}
    \left(D^2T^{(B)}(m)\{\kappa^{(B)}_3,\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\}\right)_{iabc}
\]

label: eq:one-step-conditioning-new
title: Proof
body_md:
We provide the proof for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.
    For $s\in \{\pm 1\}$, the contribution $Z_i(s)$ to the partition function from $\sigma_i = s$ is $\exp(h_i s + \phi_i(s))$.
    Thus,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:one-step-conditioning-new}
        \mathsf{arctanh}(m_i) - h_i
        = \frac12 \log \frac{1+m_i}{1-m_i} - h_i
        = \frac12 \log \frac{Z_i(+1)}{Z_i(-1)} - h_i
        = \frac{\phi_i(+1) - \phi_i(-1)}{2}.
    \end{equation}
    Differentiating \Cref{e:phi-i} yields, for $s\in \{\pm 1\}$,
    \[
        \phi'_i(s) = \beta \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top m^{(i,s)}\,.
    \]
    Combining with $m_{-i} = \frac{1+m_i}{2} m^{(i,+)} + \frac{1-m_i}{2} m^{(i,-)}$ yields
    \[
        \beta \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top m_{-i} = \frac{1+m_i}{2} \phi'_i(1) + \frac{1-m_i}{2} \phi'_i(-1)
        = \frac{\phi'_i(1) + \phi'_i(-1)}{2} + m_i \cdot \beta \boldsymbol{M}^\top_{i,-i} d_i\,.
    \]
    Substituting the last display and \Cref{eq:one-step-conditioning-new} into $r_i = T_i(m) - h_i$ yields $r_i = \zeta_i + m_i \lambda_i$.
    The second equality in \Cref{eq:zeta} follows from integration by parts.

label: eq:D2-cov-cov
title: Proof
body_md:
We provide the proof for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.
    Most of the proof will be devoted to the estimates
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:D2-cov-cov}
        \mathbf{E} \|D^2T(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^p &\leqslant C_p N^{p/2}\,, \\
        \label{eq:D2-k3-cov}
        \mathbf{E} \|D^2T(m)\{\kappa_3,\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^p &\leqslant C_p N^{3p/4}\,, \\
        \label{eq:D3-cov-cov-cov}
        \mathbf{E} \|D^3T(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^p &\leqslant C_p N^{p/2}\,.
    \end{align}
    We first explain why they imply the conclusion.
    Together with \cref{cor:r-grad23}, these imply
    \[
        \mathbf{E} \|K\kappa_3\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_p N^{p/2}\,, \qquad
        \mathbf{E} \|K\kappa_4\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_p N^{3p/4}\,.
    \]
    Let $\mathcal E = \{K\succeq\gamma\mathrm{Id}\}$, where $\gamma>0$ is given by \cref{lem:organized-gap}.
    On $\mathcal E$, for each $q\in \{3,4\}$,
    \[
        \|\kappa_q\|_F
        \leqslant \|K^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \|K\kappa_q\|_F
        \leqslant \gamma^{-1} \|K\kappa_q\|_F\,.
    \]
    while on the complement of $\mathcal E$, we can use the crude bound $\|\kappa_q\|_F \leqslant CN^{q/2}$.
    By the above and \cref{lem:organized-gap},
    \[
        \mathbf{E} \|\kappa_3\|_F^p
        \leqslant \gamma^{-p} \mathbf{E} \|K\kappa_3\|_F^p
        + \mathbf{Pr}[\mathcal E^c] C_p N^{3p/2}
        \leqslant C_p N^{p/2}\,,
    \]
    and similarly $\mathbf{E} \|\kappa_4\|_F^p \leqslant C_p N^{3p/4}$.
    We now turn to the proofs of \cref{eq:D2-cov-cov,eq:D2-k3-cov,eq:D3-cov-cov-cov}.
    Write
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:AU}
        A(z) = \mathsf{arctanh}(z)\,, \qquad
        U(z) = - \frac{\beta^2}{N} \|z\|^2 z\,,
    \end{equation}
    where $\mathsf{arctanh}$ is applied entry-wise.
    Note that $T - A - U$ is linear in $m$.
    It therefore suffices to establish \cref{eq:D2-cov-cov,eq:D2-k3-cov,eq:D3-cov-cov-cov} with $A$ and $U$ in place of $T$.

    We first treat $A$.
    Set
    \[
        y_i=v_i^{-1}\nabla m_i\,,\qquad
        z_i=v_i^{-1}\nabla^2m_i\,.
    \]
    Since $\nabla m = \mathbf{Cov}$ and $\nabla^2m = \kappa_3$, direct differentiation gives
    \begin{align*}
        \left( D^2A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i
        &= 2m_i y_i^{\otimes2}\,, \\
        \left( D^2A(m)\{\kappa_3,\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i
        &= 2m_i z_i\otimes y_i\,, \\
        \left( D^3A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i
        &= 2(1+3m_i^2)y_i^{\otimes3}\,.
    \end{align*}
    By \cref{lem:tap-derivative-estimates-new} with $j=1,2$, for every fixed $p\geqslant 2$,
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|y_i\|_2^p\leqslant C_p\,, \qquad
        \mathbf{E}\|z_i\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p/4} \,.
    \]
    Together with the trivial estimate $|m_i| \leqslant 1$ and H\"older's inequality, we obtain for all $i$
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbf{E} \left\|\left( D^2A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i\right\|_F^p
        &\leqslant C_p, \\
        \mathbf{E} \left\|\left( D^2A(m)\{\kappa_3,\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i\right\|_F^p
        &\leqslant C_p N^{p/4}\,, \\
        \mathbf{E} \left\|\left( D^3A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\} \right)_i\right\|_F^p
        &\leqslant C_p\,.
    \end{align*}
    For any tensor $H \in (\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^N)^{\otimes q}$ with slices $H_i \in (\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^N)^{\otimes (q-1)}$ along the first index, the inequality
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|H\|_F^p
        =\mathbf{E}\left(\sum_i\|H_i\|_F^2\right)^{p/2}
        \leqslant N^{p/2-1}\sum_i\mathbf{E}\|H_i\|_F^p
    \]
    therefore yields \cref{eq:D2-cov-cov,eq:D2-k3-cov,eq:D3-cov-cov-cov} with $A$ in place of $T$.
    We next treat $U$.
    Direct differentiation gives
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:D2U}
        \left(D^2U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\right)_{ijk}
        &=-\frac{2\beta^2}{N}\left(
            m_i(\mathbf{Cov}^2)_{jk}+\mathbf{Cov}_{ij}(\mathbf{Cov} m)_k+\mathbf{Cov}_{ik}(\mathbf{Cov} m)_j
        \right),\\
        \nonumber
        \left(D^2U(m)\{\kappa_3,\mathbf{Cov}\}\right)_{ijk\ell}
        &=-\frac{2\beta^2}{N}\left(
            m_i\sum_a(\kappa_3)_{ajk}\mathbf{Cov}_{a\ell}
            +(\kappa_3)_{ijk}(\mathbf{Cov} m)_\ell
            +\mathbf{Cov}_{i\ell}\sum_a m_a(\kappa_3)_{ajk}
        \right),\\
        \nonumber
        \left(D^3U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\right)_{ijk\ell}
        &=-\frac{2\beta^2}{N}\left(
            \mathbf{Cov}_{ij}(\mathbf{Cov}^2)_{k\ell}
            +\mathbf{Cov}_{ik}(\mathbf{Cov}^2)_{j\ell}
            +\mathbf{Cov}_{i\ell}(\mathbf{Cov}^2)_{jk}
        \right)\,.
    \end{align}
    The triangle inequality and Cauchy--Schwarz imply
    \begin{align*}
        \|D^2U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F
        &\leqslant\frac{6\beta^2}{N}\|m\|_2\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F^2,\\
        \|D^2U(m)\{\kappa_3,\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F
        &\leqslant\frac{6\beta^2}{N}\|m\|_2\|\kappa_3\|_F\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F,\\
        \|D^3U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F
        &\leqslant\frac{6\beta^2}{N}\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F^3\,.
    \end{align*}
    By \cref{lem:cumulant-bounds},
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p/2}\,, \qquad
        \mathbf{E}\|\kappa_3\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{3p/4}\,.
    \]
    Combining these with $\|m\|_2\leqslant\sqrt N$ and H\"older's inequality gives \cref{eq:D2-cov-cov,eq:D2-k3-cov,eq:D3-cov-cov-cov} with $U$ in place of $T$.

label: lem:improved-cumulant-cov
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:improved-cumulant-cov}
    For all $p\geqslant 2$, there exists $C_p > 0$ such that for all $|B| \leqslant 2$,
    \[
        \mathbf{E} \|\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^p
        \leqslant C_p \,.
    \]
    In particular, \cref{lem:improved-cumulant}\ref{it:improved-cumulant-cov} follows as the case $|B| \leqslant 1$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We provide the proof for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.
    Let $\mathcal E = \{K\succeq\gamma\mathrm{Id}\}$, where $\gamma>0$ is given by \cref{lem:organized-gap}.
    On $\mathcal E$, the identity $K\mathbf{Cov}=\mathrm{Id}+\nabla r$ from \cref{fac:improved-cumulant-start} gives
    \[
        \|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
        \leqslant \|K^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\mathrm{Id}+\nabla r\|_{\mathrm{op}}
        \leqslant \gamma^{-1}\left(1+\|\nabla r\|_F\right)\,.
    \]
    On the complement of $\mathcal E$, we use the crude bound
    \[
        \|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant\Tr\mathbf{Cov}=\sum_i(1-m_i^2)\leqslant N\,.
    \]
    Thus,
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbf{E}\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^p
        &\leqslant \gamma^{-p}\mathbf{E} \left[\left(1 + \|\nabla r\|_F\right)^p\right]
        +N^p\mathbf{Pr}[\mathcal E^c] \\
        &\leqslant 2^{p-1} \gamma^{-p} \left(1 + \mathbf{E} \|\nabla r\|_F^p \right)
        +N^p\mathbf{Pr}[\mathcal E^c]\,.
    \end{align*}
    By \cref{cor:r-grad12} and \cref{lem:organized-gap}, this is bounded by $C_p$.

label: eq:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob-goal
title: Proof
body_md:
We will show that there exists a universal $C>0$ such that for all $a>0$, there exists $C_a > 0$ such that uniformly over $B$ with $|B| \leqslant 2$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob-goal}
        \mathbf{Pr}[\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(B)}\|_F > C\sqrt N] \leqslant C_a N^{-a}\,.
    \end{equation} 
    The conclusion follows from \cref{eq:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob-goal} by a union bound (and adjusting $a$).
    We provide the proof of \cref{eq:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob-goal} for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.

    Let $\gamma>0$ be given by \cref{lem:organized-gap} and set $\mathcal E = \{K\succeq\gamma\mathrm{Id}\}$.
    On $\mathcal E$, \cref{fac:improved-cumulant-start} gives
    \[
        \|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F
        \leqslant \|K^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\mathrm{Id}+\nabla r\|_F
        \leqslant \gamma^{-1}\left(\sqrt N+\|\nabla r\|_F\right)\,.
    \]
    Take $p\geqslant\max(2,2a)$.
    By Markov's inequality, \cref{cor:r-grad12}, and \cref{lem:organized-gap},
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbf{Pr}\left[\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F>2\gamma^{-1}\sqrt N\right]
        &\leqslant \mathbf{Pr}[\mathcal E^c]
        +\mathbf{Pr}\left[\|\nabla r\|_F>\sqrt N\right] \\
        &\leqslant \mathbf{Pr}[\mathcal E^c]
        +N^{-p/2}\mathbf{E}\|\nabla r\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_a N^{-a}\,.
    \end{align*}
    This proves \cref{eq:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob-goal} with $C=2\gamma^{-1}$.

body_md:

    For all $p\geqslant 2$, there exists $C_p > 0$ such that for all $|B|\leqslant 1$,

        \max_{i\in [N] \setminus B}
        \mathbf{E} \left|\|d_i^{(B)}\|_2^2 - \frac{\beta^2}{N} \|\mathbf{Cov}^{(B \cup \{i\})}\|_F^2 \right|^p

label: lem:di-concentration-step1
title: Proof
body_md:
We provide the proof for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.
    Fix $i\in[N]$ and set 
    \[
        \epsilon_i = d_i - \beta\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}\,, \qquad 
        H_i = (\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)})^2\,.
    \]
    Note that $v_i^{-1} \nabla m_i = v_i^{-1} \mathbf{Cov}_i$ has $1$ in its $i$-th entry, and its remaining entries are $d_i$.
    Thus \cref{lem:tap-derivative-estimates-new} implies, for every $p\geqslant2$,
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|d_i\|_2^p\leqslant C_p\,,\qquad
        \mathbf{E}\|\epsilon_i\|_2^p\leqslant C_pN^{-p/2}\,.
    \]
    Note that
    \[
        \|d_i\|_2^2-\beta^2\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top H_i\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}
        = \|d_i\|_2^2-\|d_i-\epsilon_i\|_2^2
        = 2\langle d_i,\epsilon_i\rangle - \|\epsilon_i\|_2^2\,.
    \]
    By H\"older's inequality,
    \begin{equation}\label{lem:di-concentration-step1}
        \mathbf{E}\left|\|d_i\|_2^2-\beta^2\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top H_i\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}\right|^p
        \leqslant C_pN^{-p/2}\,.
    \end{equation}
    Conditional on $({\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{W}_{-i,-i},\boldsymbol{g})$, the matrix $H_i$ is fixed and
    \[
        \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}=\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}+\eta_i\,,\qquad
        \eta_i=\frac{\beta{\boldsymbol{x}}_i{\boldsymbol{x}}_{-i}}{N}\,,
    \]
    where $\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}\sim\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{Id}/N)$ and $\|\eta_i\|_2\leqslant\frac{\beta}{\sqrt N}$.
    Writing $\mathbf{E}_i$ for expectation over $\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}$ under this conditioning, standard Gaussian quadratic- and linear-form moment bounds give
    \[
        \mathbf{E}_i\left|\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top H_i\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}-\frac{\Tr H_i}{N}\right|^p
        \leqslant \frac{C_p}{N^p} \|H_i\|_F^p
        +\frac{\|H_i\eta_i\|_2^p}{N^{p/2}}
        +|\eta_i^\top H_i\eta_i|^p
        \leqslant \frac{C_p}{N^p} \|H_i\|_F^p\,.
    \]
    Since $\|H_i\|_F\leqslant\sqrt N\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2$, \cref{lem:improved-cumulant-cov} implies
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\left|\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top H_i\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}-\frac{\Tr H_i}{N}\right|^p
        \leqslant C_pN^{-p/2}\,.
    \]
    Combining with \cref{lem:di-concentration-step1} and $\Tr H_i=\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\|_F^2$ proves the result.

label: eq:improved-cumulant-kappa3-high-prob-goal
title: Proof
body_md:
We will show that there exists a universal $C>0$ such that for all $a>0$, there exists $C_a>0$ such that uniformly over $B$ with $|B|\leqslant 1$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:improved-cumulant-kappa3-high-prob-goal}
        \mathbf{Pr}[\|\kappa_3^{(B)}\|_F>C\sqrt N]\leqslant C_aN^{-a}\,.
    \end{equation}
    The conclusion follows by a union bound (and adjusting $a$).
    We provide the proof of \cref{eq:improved-cumulant-kappa3-high-prob-goal} for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.

    Let $A,U$ be defined as in \eqref{eq:AU}; as observed in the proof of \cref{lem:improved-cumulant-kappa34}, $T - A - U$ is linear.
    By \cref{fac:improved-cumulant-start},
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:improved-cumulant-kappa3-high-prob-start}
        K\kappa_3 = \nabla^2 r - D^2 A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\} - D^2 U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\,.
    \end{equation}
    By \cref{eq:D2U} and the estimates $\|m\|_2 \leqslant \sqrt{N}$, $\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F \leqslant \sqrt{N} \|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$,
    \[
        \|D^2U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F
        \leqslant \frac{6\beta^2}{N}\|m\|_2\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_F
        \leqslant 6\beta^2\|\mathbf{Cov}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\,.
    \]
    Together with \cref{cor:r-grad12,lem:improved-cumulant-cov}, this implies, for every fixed $p\geqslant 2$,
    \[
        \max\left\{
            \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^2 r\|_F^p,
            \mathbf{E}\|D^2U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^p
        \right\} \leqslant C_pN^{p/4}\,.
    \]
    By Markov's inequality with $p\geqslant\max(2,4a)$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:grad2r-D2U-high-prob-ub}
        \mathbf{Pr}\left(
            \max(\|\nabla^2 r\|_F, \|D^2U(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F)
            \geqslant \sqrt{N}
        \right) \leqslant C_a N^{-a}\,.
    \end{equation}
    We turn to controlling the term $\|D^2 A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F$.
    As noted in the proof of \cref{lem:di-concentration}, the $i$-th coordinate of $v_i^{-1}\nabla m_i$ is $1$, and the remaining coordinates are $d_i$.
    So,
    \[
        \|D^2A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^2
        = 4\sum_i m_i^2\|v_i^{-1}\nabla m_i\|_2^4
        \leqslant 4\sum_i(1+\|d_i\|_2^2)^2\,.
    \]
    Set $q_i = \beta^2 \|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\|_F^2 / N$ and
    \[
        \Gamma = \sum_i \left|\|d_i\|_2^2 - q_i \right|^2\,.
    \]
    By Jensen's inequality and \cref{lem:di-concentration}, for every $p\geqslant 1$,
    \[
        \mathbf{E} \Gamma^p
        \leqslant N^{p-1} \sum_i \mathbf{E} \left|\|d_i\|_2^2 - q_i \right|^{2p}
        \leqslant C_p\,.
    \]
    By Markov's inequality with $p \geqslant \max(1,a)$, $\mathbf{Pr}(\Gamma \leqslant N) \geqslant 1 - C_a N^{-a}$.
    \cref{lem:improved-cumulant-cov-high-prob} provides a universal constant $C_0$ such that
    \[
        \mathbf{Pr}(\max_i q_i \leqslant \beta^2 C_0^2)
        \geqslant 1 - C_a N^{-a}\,.
    \]
    On the intersection of these two events,
    \[
        \|D^2A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F^2
        \leqslant 4 \sum_i(1+\|d_i\|_2^2)^2
        \leqslant 8\sum_i (1 + q_i)^2 + 8\Gamma
        \leqslant 8N\left((1 + \beta^2 C_0^2)^2 + 1\right)\,.
    \]
    This provides an absolute $C$ such that
    \[
        \mathbf{Pr}(\|D^2A(m)\{\mathbf{Cov},\mathbf{Cov}\}\|_F > C\sqrt{N}) \leqslant C_a N^{-a}\,.
    \]
    Recalling \eqref{eq:improved-cumulant-kappa3-high-prob-start}, a union bound with \cref{eq:grad2r-D2U-high-prob-ub} shows
    \[
        \mathbf{Pr}(\|K\kappa_3\|_F > C \sqrt{N}) \leqslant C_a N^{-a}\,,
    \]
    after adjusting $C$ and $C_a$.
    Combining with \cref{lem:organized-gap} proves the result.

title: Proof
body_md:
We provide the proof for $B = \emptyset$ and omit the superscript $(\emptyset)$; the case of general $B$ is analogous.
    The proof proceeds in five steps, and uses only \cref{lem:cumulant-bounds,lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} and Gaussian moment estimates.

    \textit{Step 1: cavity expansion for $d_i$.}
    Let $\epsilon_i = d_i - \beta \mathbf{Cov}^{(i)} \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}$. In this step we prove
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-derivative-estimates-new-step1}
        \mathbf{E}\|\epsilon_i\|_2^p\leqslant C_pN^{-p/2}\,,
    \end{equation}
    which is the first estimate of the lemma.
    For $s' \in \{\pm 1\}$, Taylor expansion gives
    \[
        m^{(i,s')}
        = \nabla F^{(i)}(u_i + s'\beta \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i})
        = \nabla F^{(i)}(u_i)
        + s' \beta \mathbf{Cov}^{(i)} \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}
        + \frac{\beta^2}{2} \kappa_3^{(i)} [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes 2}]
        + \epsilon_{i,s'},
    \]
    where
    \[
        \epsilon_{i,s'} = \frac{s'\beta^3}{2}\int_0^1(1-s)^2
        \kappa_{4,ss'}^{(i)} [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes 3}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \]
    Thus
    \[
        d_i = \frac{m^{(i,+)}-m^{(i,-)}}{2}
        = \beta \mathbf{Cov}^{(i)} \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i} + \frac{\epsilon_{i,+} - \epsilon_{i,-}}{2}\,,
    \]
    and
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-d-taylor-remainder}
        \epsilon_i = \frac{\epsilon_{i,+} - \epsilon_{i,-}}{2}
        =\frac{\beta^3}{4}\int_0^1(1-s)^2
        \left(\kappa_{4,s}^{(i)}+\kappa_{4,-s}^{(i)}\right)
        [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes3}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \end{equation}
    Applying \cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} with $r=4$, $k=0$, and $\ell=3$ yields \cref{eq:tap-derivative-estimates-new-step1}.
    
    \textit{Step 2: moments of $d_i$ and its derivatives.}
    In this step, we prove the auxiliary estimate
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-d-derivatives-aux}
        \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j d_i\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{pj/4}
    \end{equation}
    for $j=0,1,2,3$.
    Conditional on $({\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{W}_{-i,-i},\boldsymbol{g})$, the matrix $\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}$ is fixed and
    \[
        \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}=\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}+\eta_i\,,\qquad
        \eta_i=\frac{\beta{\boldsymbol{x}}_i{\boldsymbol{x}}_{-i}}{N}\,,
    \]
    where $\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i} \sim \mathcal N(0, \mathrm{Id}/N)$ and $\|\eta_i\|_2 \leqslant \beta / \sqrt{N}$.
    Write $\mathbf{E}_i$ for expectation over $\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}$ under this conditioning.
    Gaussian moments give
    \[
        \mathbf{E}_i\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}\|_2^p
        \leqslant \frac{C_p}{N^{p/2}}\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\|_F^p
        + \|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\eta_i\|_2^p
        \leqslant \frac{C_p}{N^{p/2}}\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\|_F^p\,.
    \]
    Taking expectation and using the covariance bound from \cref{lem:cumulant-bounds}, we obtain
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}\|_2^p\leqslant C_p
    \]
    Together with \cref{eq:tap-derivative-estimates-new-step1} this implies \cref{eq:tap-d-derivatives-aux} for $j=0$.
    For $j=1,2,3$, differentiating $d_i=(m^{(i,+)}-m^{(i,-)})/2$ and then integrating in $s$ gives
    \[
        \nabla^j d_i
        =\frac{\kappa_{j+1,1}^{(i)}-\kappa_{j+1,-1}^{(i)}}2
        =\frac\beta2\int_{-1}^1
        \kappa_{j+2,s}^{(i)}[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \]
    Applying \cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} with $r=j+2$, $k=0$, and $\ell=1$ proves \cref{eq:tap-d-derivatives-aux}.

    \textit{Step 3: derivatives of $m_i$ and $\zeta_i$.}
    In this step we prove the lemma's estimates on $(v_i)^{-1} \nabla^j m_i$ and $\nabla^j \zeta_i$.
    Set $a_i=\mathsf{arctanh}(m_i)$.
    By the definition of $d_i$,
    \[
        \nabla a_i=v_i^{-1}\nabla m_i=v_i^{-1}\mathbf{Cov}_i=(1,d_i),
    \]
    where we write the $i$-th coordinate first.
    Differentiating this identity and using \cref{eq:tap-d-derivatives-aux} gives
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-a-derivatives-aux}
        \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j a_i\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p(j-1)/4}
    \end{equation}
    for $j=1,2,3$.
    Since $m_i=\tanh a_i$ and $v_i=1-m_i^2$, we calculate
    \[
        \frac{\tanh'(a_i)}{v_i}=1\,,\qquad
        \frac{\tanh''(a_i)}{v_i}=-2m_i\,,\qquad
        \frac{\tanh'''(a_i)}{v_i}=6m_i^2-2\,.
    \]
    Thus the chain rule gives
    \begin{align*}
        v_i^{-1}\nabla m_i
        &=\nabla a_i\,,\\
        v_i^{-1}\nabla^2m_i
        &=\nabla^2a_i-2m_i(\nabla a_i)^{\otimes2}\,,\\
        v_i^{-1}\nabla^3m_i
        &=\nabla^3a_i-2m_i\sum_{\mathsf{Sym}}\nabla^2a_i\otimes\nabla a_i
        +(6m_i^2-2)(\nabla a_i)^{\otimes3}\,.
    \end{align*}
    Since $|m_i|\leqslant1$, all coefficients are bounded.
    Applying \cref{eq:tap-a-derivatives-aux} proves the desired estimates on $v_i^{-1}\nabla^j m_i$.
    Finally, differentiating the integral representation in \cref{eq:zeta} yields
    \[
        \nabla^j\zeta_i
        =-\frac{\beta^3}{4}\int_{-1}^1(1-s^2)
        \kappa_{j+3,s}^{(i)}[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes3}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \]
    Applying \cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} with $r=j+3$, $k=0$, and $\ell=3$ proves the claimed estimates on $\nabla^j\zeta_i$.
    
    \textit{Step 4: cavity estimate for covariance trace.}
    Set $\Xi_i=\Tr\mathbf{Cov}-\Tr\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}$.
    In this step, we prove the auxiliary estimate
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-cavity-trace-derivatives}
        \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j\Xi_i\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p(j+1)/4}
    \end{equation}
    for $j=0,1,2,3$.
    Note that here, $\nabla$ includes derivatives in coordinate $i$ of the external field $u = h$, even though $\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}$ does not depend on this coordinate.

    Let $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ be a sample from the Gibbs measure.
    The law of total covariance yields
    \begin{align*}
        \Xi_i
        &= \Tr \mathbf{E}[\mathbf{Cov}(\boldsymbol{\sigma} | \sigma_i)] 
        - \Tr \mathbf{Cov}^{(i)} 
        + \Tr \mathbf{Cov}(\mathbf{E}[\boldsymbol{\sigma} | \sigma_i]) \\
        &= \frac{1+m_i}{2} \kappa_{2,1}^{(i)}[\mathrm{Id}]
        + \frac{1-m_i}{2} \kappa_{2,-1}^{(i)}[\mathrm{Id}]
        - \kappa_2^{(i)}[\mathrm{Id}]
        + v_i(1+\|d_i\|_2^2)
        = \frac12 \Xi_{i,1} + \frac{m_i}{2} \Xi_{i,2} 
        + v_i(1+\|d_i\|_2^2)\,,
    \end{align*}
    where
    \[
        \Xi_{i,1} = \left(\kappa_{2,1}^{(i)} + \kappa_{2,-1}^{(i)} - 2 \kappa_2^{(i)}\right)[\mathrm{Id}]\,,\qquad
        \Xi_{i,2} = \left(\kappa_{2,1}^{(i)} - \kappa_{2,-1}^{(i)}\right)[\mathrm{Id}]\,.
    \]
    For $j=0,1,2,3$, Taylor expansion in $s$ gives
    \begin{align*}
        \nabla^j \Xi_{i,1}
        = \left(
            \kappa_{j+2,1}^{(i)}
            + \kappa_{j+2,-1}^{(i)}
            - 2\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}
        \right)[\mathrm{Id}]
        &=\beta^2\int_0^1(1-s)
        \left(
            \kappa_{j+4,s}^{(i)}
            +\kappa_{j+4,-s}^{(i)}
        \right)
        [\mathrm{Id}\otimes\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s,\\
        \nabla^j \Xi_{i,2} = \left(
            \kappa_{j+2,1}^{(i)}
            -\kappa_{j+2,-1}^{(i)}
        \right)[\mathrm{Id}]
        &=\beta\int_{-1}^1
        \kappa_{j+3,s}^{(i)}[\mathrm{Id}\otimes\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \end{align*}
    Applying \cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} with $(r,k,\ell)=(j+4,1,2)$ and $(j+3,1,1)$ respectively, and integrating in $s$, bounds
    \[
        \mathbf{E} \|\nabla^j \Xi_{i,1}\|_F^p \leqslant C_p N^{pj/4}\,,\qquad
        \mathbf{E} \|\nabla^j \Xi_{i,2}\|_F^p \leqslant C_p N^{p(j+1)/4}\,.
    \]
    From the conclusion of step 3 and the trivial bound $v_i \leqslant 1$, we have $\mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j m_i\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p(j-1)/4}$ for $j=1,2,3$.
    Differentiating $v_i=1-m_i^2$ gives the same bound for $\nabla^j v_i$; thus
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-m-v-derivatives-aux}
        \max\left\{
            \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j m_i\|_F^p\,,
            \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j v_i\|_F^p
        \right\}
        \leqslant C_pN^{p(j-1)/4}
    \end{equation}
    for $j=1,2,3$.
                      
    Combining \cref{eq:tap-d-derivatives-aux,eq:tap-m-v-derivatives-aux} with $0\leqslant v_i\leqslant1$ yields
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\left\|\nabla^j\left(v_i(1+\|d_i\|_2^2)\right)\right\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_pN^{pj/4}
    \]
    for $j=0,1,2,3$.
    Together this proves \cref{eq:tap-cavity-trace-derivatives}.

    \textit{Step 5: derivatives of $\lambda_i$.}
    In this step we prove the lemma's estimates on $\nabla^j\lambda_i$.
    Using $\Tr\mathbf{Cov}=N-\|m\|_2^2$ and the definitions $\epsilon_i = d_i - \beta\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}$ from Step 1 and $\Xi_i = \Tr \mathbf{Cov} - \Tr \mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}$ from Step 4, we obtain
    \[
        \lambda_i
        =\frac{\beta^2}{N}\Tr\mathbf{Cov}-\beta\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top d_i
        =\frac{\beta^2}{N}\Xi_i
        -\beta^2\mathbf{Cov}^{(i)}\left[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}\right]
        -\beta\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top\epsilon_i\,.
    \]
    Differentiating with respect to the external field gives
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:tap-centered-lambda-derivatives}
        \nabla^j\lambda_i
        =\frac{\beta^2}{N}\nabla^j\Xi_i
        -\beta^2\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}
        \left[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}\right]
        -\beta\nabla^j(\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top\epsilon_i)\,,
    \end{equation}
    for $j=0,1,2,3$.
    Since $\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}$ does not depend on the external field, differentiating \cref{eq:tap-d-taylor-remainder} gives
    \[
        \nabla^j(\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top\epsilon_i)
        = \frac{\beta^3}{4}
        \int_0^1(1-s)^2
        \left(\kappa_{j+4,s}^{(i)}+\kappa_{j+4,-s}^{(i)}\right)
        [\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes4}]\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} s\,.
    \]
    By \cref{lem:cumulant-contraction-estimates} with $r=j+4$, $k=0$, and $\ell=4$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:grad-Meps}
        \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j(\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^\top\epsilon_i)\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p(j-4)/4}\,.
    \end{equation}
    We will bound the $\nabla^j \Xi_i$ term in \cref{eq:tap-centered-lambda-derivatives} using \cref{eq:tap-cavity-trace-derivatives}.
    We now turn to the $\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}$ term.
    Recall from Step 2 the notation $\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}=\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}+\eta_i$, and that $\mathbf{E}_i$ denotes expectation over $\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}$ conditional on $({\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{W}_{-i,-i},\boldsymbol{g})$.
    Then
    \[
        \boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}
        =\left(\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}\right)
        +\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}\otimes\eta_i+\eta_i\otimes\boldsymbol{W}_{i,-i}
        +\eta_i^{\otimes2}\,.
    \]
    For any tensor $H$ of order at least two measurable with respect to $({\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{W}_{-i,-i},\boldsymbol{g})$, Gaussian quadratic- and linear-form moment bounds give
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbf{E}_i\left\|H\left[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}\right]\right\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_p\left(\frac1N+\frac{\|\eta_i\|_2}{\sqrt N}+\|\eta_i\|_2^2\right)^p \|H\|_F^p
        \leqslant\frac{C_p}{N^p}\|H\|_F^p\,.
    \end{align*}
    The last inequality uses $\|\eta_i\|_2\leqslant\beta/\sqrt N$ from Step 2.
    Taking $H=\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}$, which is fixed under the conditioning, and taking expectation yields
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\left\|\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}
        \left[\boldsymbol{M}_{i,-i}^{\otimes2}-\frac{\mathrm{Id}}{N}\right]\right\|_F^p
        \leqslant\frac{C_p}{N^p}\mathbf{E}\|\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}\|_F^p\,.
    \]
    Combining this with \cref{eq:tap-cavity-trace-derivatives,eq:tap-centered-lambda-derivatives,eq:grad-Meps} proves
    \[
        \mathbf{E}\|\nabla^j\lambda_i\|_F^p
        \leqslant C_p\left(N^{p(j-3)/4}+N^{-p}\mathbf{E}\|\kappa_{j+2}^{(i)}\|_F^p\right)
    \]
    for $j=0,1,2,3$, as desired.
    If $j=0$, \cref{lem:cumulant-bounds} gives $\mathbf{E}\|\kappa_2^{(i)}\|_F^p\leqslant C_pN^{p/2}$, and we obtain the final assertion $\mathbf{E}|\lambda_i|^p \leqslant C_pN^{-p/2}$ of the lemma.
